classification.difficultyReason: Solve two linear equations and verify that their unique intersection also lies on a third line.

content.prompt: Prove that the lines $2y-x=2$, $y+x=7$ and $y=2x-5$ are concurrent. (That is, they intersect at only one point.)

answer.short:
The three lines are concurrent at $(4,3)$.

Solve the first two equations and check that their intersection satisfies the third.
answer.worked:
Adding $2y-x=2$ and $y+x=7$ gives:
$$\begin{align*}3y&=9\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
Substituting into $y+x=7$:
$$\begin{align*}3+x&=7\\x&=4\end{align*}$$
Check $(4,3)$ in all three equations:
$$\begin{align*}2(3)-4&=2\\3+4&=7\\3&=2(4)-5\end{align*}$$
The first two equations have the unique solution $(4,3)$, which also satisfies the third equation. Therefore, the three lines are concurrent at $(4,3)$.
